issues.item: Rehearse Conversations: rehearse what to say before any interaction
issues.explanation: This strategy is socially anxious/interpersonal in content and is hard to integrate with the rest of the profile, which is dominated by war-zone danger cues, hypervigilant threat monitoring, and trauma-memory reactivation. The other strategies and threat/memory items coherently reflect trauma-related safety management, but rehearsing conversations before any interaction targets a different problem domain that is not represented elsewhere in Triggers, Threat, or Memory. Given the formulation, maladaptive strategies should plausibly feed back into triggers/threat/memory; this item does not connect well to those active nodes.

vignette: Marcus is a 29-year-old North American man who worked as a relief worker in a war zone before returning to his occupation as a jeweler. His experience has left him with a complex web of symptoms that have significantly impacted his life. During his time as a relief worker, Marcus was caught in the crossfire of an intense battle while delivering supplies to refugees. The chaos and danger were overwhelming; he vividly remembers the sound of children crying in fear, the pounding of his own heart, and the unexpected touch from others trying to help him find shelter. These experiences have become potent triggers for him. Marcus has developed a heightened sensitivity to certain stimuli that remind him of those traumatic moments. For instance, the sound of kids crying can instantly bring back the full memory of that horrific day, overwhelming him with an intense emotional response without any clear visual image accompanying it. The feeling is so real and vivid that he often finds himself unable to distinguish between his current reality and the memories from the war zone. The presence of these triggers has led Marcus to employ several maladaptive strategies in an attempt to cope. He constantly scans his surroundings for signs of threat, ensuring his back is always against a wall where he can see everything around him. Even when others assure him that he’s safe, he finds it nearly impossible to believe them. This constant vigilance and fear have made his memories even more intrusive. For example, during one particularly busy day at work, Marcus heard the sound of children crying from a nearby playground. Instantly, he was transported back to the war zone, feeling his heart race as if he were in danger again. The intensity of this reaction compelled him to leave his workstation and seek a quiet place where he could regain some sense of control. To manage these overwhelming experiences, Marcus has developed several maladaptive strategies. He frequently engages in positive reframing, forcing himself to think only positive thoughts whenever the memories surface. However, these efforts often lead to feelings of guilt and inadequacy, reinforcing his belief that he should be able to handle things better. Additionally, he relies on downward comparison, reminding himself that it could have been worse, but this reasoning doesn’t provide lasting relief. The cycle of triggers, memory intrusions, and maladaptive strategies has become increasingly self-reinforcing over time. For instance, when Marcus feels his heart racing while at work, the memory of the battle is triggered, causing him to feel even more unsafe. This heightened sense of threat then leads him to scan his environment more intensely for potential dangers, further reinforcing his belief that he cannot trust his safety. Despite these efforts, Marcus’s symptoms have only intensified over time. His constant vigilance and avoidance behaviors have strained his relationships with colleagues and friends. He has become increasingly isolated, finding it difficult to engage in social activities or even go about his daily routines without being reminded of the trauma. What finally brought Marcus to seek help was a particularly distressing incident at work where he had a panic attack while working on an intricate piece of jewelry. The sound of a child crying nearby triggered the full memory of the war zone, causing him to drop tools and flee the shop in a state of sheer terror. This event left him feeling humiliated and deeply afraid that he might not be able to continue his work. Marcus is most hopeful for relief from these overwhelming memories and triggers so that he can regain control over his life and relationships. He is most afraid that the trauma will continue to dictate how he experiences the world, leaving him trapped in a cycle of fear and isolation.
